newsitem.title: FRANCE: Rail strike cripples traffic in Marseille.
newsitem.headline: Rail strike cripples traffic in Marseille.

text.p: A rail strike over proposed job cuts slashed train service on southeastern France for the fifth day on Friday, transport officials said.
Traffic out of Marseille's main Saint Charles station was paralysed after railworkers blocked the tracks a few km (miles) out of the station.
Talks between the state rail company SNCF and the strikers broke down on Thursday and the protesters decided to stiffen the stoppage.
SNCF management has said the tracks must be cleared before negotiations could be resumed and did not rule out calling in police to take the strikers away by force.
The SNCF suggested that passengers get off their trains at Marseille's other two stations where bus service has been put in place.
Elsewhere in the southeast, long-distance trains were mildly disrupted, but up to 80 percent of regional trains were cancelled.

A separate transport workers strike in Paris to demand staff and wage hikes slightly disrupted the city's metro services. The Paris transport authority RATP said traffic was curtailed by up to 30 percent at mid-morning on three of the capital's 13 metro lines.

The two most powerful SNCF unions have asked members to join a nationwide strike called for October 17 by civil service unions to press for a pay raises and protest against the centre-right government's plans to cut 6,000 jobs next year.
Railworkers led a crippling 24-day public sector strike late last year when Prime Minister Alain Juppe proposed ending early pension rights -- plans which have since been scrapped.

The concern this time is over programmed job cuts and a modernisation plan under which the government will take 125 billion francs ($25 billion) of debt off the loss-making SNCF by spinning it off into another state company which would also become owner of the track and other infrastructure.
Unions fear the plan could open the way to additional staff cuts or a possible privatisation of the SNCF.
